subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add core pace-aware provider usage controls for autonomous agents, and should the first step be observability-only or include opt-in enforcement?
rationale: The remaining work adds provider-specific semantics, persisted usage state, new agent config, and autonomous throttling behavior that source inspection cannot safely choose without product direction.

options.title: Phase observability first
options.body: Capture and expose provider pace context in status and session surfaces without blocking agent or subagent work until the data model proves reliable.

options.title: Add opt-in enforcement now
options.body: Introduce disabled-by-default pace thresholds that can throttle subagents, with explicit config, tests, and operator recovery guidance.

options.title: Design plugin/API seam first
options.body: Keep core lean by first defining provider and agent hooks so a plugin or provider-owned module can own pace policy without hardcoding Anthropic behavior broadly in core.

recommendation.title: Phase observability first
recommendation.body: Capture and expose provider pace context in status and session surfaces without blocking agent or subagent work until the data model proves reliable.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal across provider usage and subagent boundary code touched by this decision.
